stem: Instances in a cloud VPC have no public IP addresses but must reach internet destinations. Which component performs the outbound address translation?
explanation: A NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and translates the private source addresses of instances in private subnets as their traffic leaves the VPC. Return traffic is mapped back to the originating instance, so no inbound path is created.

choices.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
An internet gateway alone
A route table local entry
A security group outbound rule

stem: In a site-to-site VPN between an on-premises network and a cloud provider, which device is represented by the customer gateway object?
explanation: The customer gateway is the cloud-side reference to the customer's own VPN endpoint, normally the on-premises router or firewall that terminates the tunnel. The virtual private gateway is the provider-side endpoint.

choices.text: The on-premises router or firewall terminating the tunnel
The provider-side VPN concentrator
The cloud NAT instance
The provider's internet gateway

stem: An access point is mounted where no power outlet exists. Which connection supplies both data and electrical power to the AP?
explanation: The AP's Ethernet uplink connects to a switch port that delivers Power over Ethernet, so a single cable carries the CAPWAP or management traffic and the DC power the AP needs. A local power injector achieves the same result when the switch cannot supply PoE.

choices.text: The Ethernet uplink to a PoE-capable switch port
The console port
A USB service port
The 5 GHz radio interface

stem: Where is an edge firewall normally placed in a campus topology?
explanation: The edge firewall sits between the ISP handoff and the internal network so every packet entering or leaving the site is inspected and filtered. Placing it inside the core would leave the WAN link itself unprotected.

choices.text: Between the ISP handoff and the internal network
Between the access and distribution layers
On each access switch uplink
Inside the data center between servers

stem: Widening a 5 GHz channel from 20 MHz to 40 MHz raises the theoretical throughput. What is the main cost of that change?
explanation: Bonding two 20 MHz channels consumes twice the spectrum, which halves the number of non-overlapping channels available in the band. In a dense deployment the wider channels overlap more often, so co-channel interference and retries increase.

choices.text: Fewer non-overlapping channels, so more co-channel interference
Lower client transmit power
Loss of WPA2 support
Inability to use 802.11ac

stem: How does an 802.11 station confirm that a unicast data frame arrived intact?
explanation: The receiving station waits a short interframe space and returns an acknowledgement frame. If the sender does not receive that ACK it assumes loss and retransmits, which is why wireless throughput falls quickly as retries climb.

choices.text: The receiver returns an ACK frame after a short interframe space
The sender waits for a TCP acknowledgement from the client
The access point broadcasts a delivery report
The frame's FCS is echoed back in the next beacon

stem: A host sends a packet to a destination on a different subnet. Whose MAC address does it place in the frame?
explanation: The host compares the destination against its own mask, sees that the target is off-subnet, and forwards the frame to its default gateway. The destination IP stays the remote host, but the frame carries the gateway MAC so the local segment can deliver it.

choices.text: The default gateway MAC address
The remote destination MAC address
The broadcast MAC address
Its own MAC address

stem: Which dotted-decimal subnet mask corresponds to a /21 prefix?
explanation: A /21 keeps 21 network bits, so the mask has 21 ones followed by 11 zeros: 255.255.248.0. The third octet contributes 11111000 in binary, which is 248.

stem: What is the principal trade-off of a collapsed-core campus design?
explanation: Collapsing distribution and core into one layer cuts cost, cabling, and hop count, but the same devices now carry all inter-VLAN and WAN traffic. Failure of a collapsed-core switch removes redundancy for a large portion of the campus and limits how far the design can scale.

choices.text: Lower cost and fewer hops, but reduced redundancy and scaling headroom
Higher cost but simpler troubleshooting
Better wireless roaming but no wired VLAN support
Guaranteed loop-free topology without STP

stem: A laptop is moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 20 but keeps its old VLAN 10 address. Why does it not simply obtain a new address immediately?
explanation: A DHCP client keeps its lease and first tries to renew at the 50 percent timer by unicasting to the original server. That server is no longer reachable in the new broadcast domain, so the client must wait for renewal to fail or be told to release before it broadcasts a fresh discovery.

choices.text: It renews at the 50 percent timer and the old server is unreachable in the new VLAN
The switch rewrites the source MAC so DHCP cannot match the request
ARP caching prevents any broadcast from being sent
The default gateway blocks all UDP traffic

stem: A router shows an ARP entry in the incomplete state for a next hop. What does that state tell you?
explanation: Incomplete means the router sent ARP requests but received no reply, so it has no MAC address to build the frame with. Packets destined through that next hop are dropped until resolution succeeds.

choices.text: No ARP reply was received, so frames to that next hop cannot be built
The entry is cached but expired and will refresh from the routing table
The next hop resolved to a multicast MAC address
The interface is administratively down

stem: What reach does Category 6A twisted-pair cabling support for 10GBASE-T?
explanation: Cat 6A is specified for 10GBASE-T over a 100-meter channel because its improved shielding and reduced alien crosstalk keep the signal usable at 500 MHz. Cat 6 is limited to about 55 meters for the same speed.

choices.text: 100 meters
55 meters
220 meters
500 meters

stem: Why are the pairs inside unshielded twisted-pair cable twisted around each other?
explanation: The twist rate differs per pair so that externally induced noise and crosstalk from neighbouring pairs couple equally into both conductors. Because the interference appears as a common-mode signal, it cancels at the receiver instead of corrupting the differential data signal.

choices.text: So induced noise couples equally into both wires and cancels at the receiver
To increase the cable's tensile strength
To allow the pairs to carry DC power
To reduce the cable's capacitance to the building ground

stem: How does TCP slow start increase the amount of data a sender may have in flight?
explanation: The sender begins with a small congestion window and grows it by roughly one segment per acknowledgement, effectively doubling the window each round-trip time. Growth continues until the window reaches the slow-start threshold or a loss is detected.

choices.text: The congestion window doubles each round-trip until the slow-start threshold
The receive window is fixed and the sender fills it immediately
The sender retransmits every segment twice to measure loss
The window grows by one segment per second regardless of acknowledgements

stem: A TCP receiver gets segments 5, 6, 8, and 9 after already receiving segment 4. What does it send back, and why?
explanation: The receiver buffers the out-of-order segments and keeps returning duplicate acknowledgements for the last in-order byte, which is segment 4's sequence space. After three duplicate ACKs the sender treats the gap as lost and retransmits segment 7 without waiting for a timer.

choices.text: Duplicate ACKs for the missing segment, which trigger a fast retransmit
A reset, because out-of-order delivery is always fatal
ACKs for segments 8 and 9, discarding segment 7
Nothing until the retransmission timer expires

stem: In a split-MAC wireless architecture, how do the CAPWAP control and data paths differ by default?
explanation: The control tunnel runs over UDP 5246 and is DTLS-encrypted to protect management exchanges between AP and controller. The data tunnel uses UDP 5247 and is not encrypted by default, because the client payload is usually already protected by 802.11 encryption.

choices.text: Control uses UDP 5246 and is DTLS-encrypted; data uses UDP 5247 and is unencrypted by default
Both tunnels share UDP 5246 and are encrypted by default
Control uses TCP 5246 and data uses TCP 5247
Data uses UDP 5246 and control uses UDP 5247, both in clear text

stem: What is a likely effect of setting the MAC address-table aging time very low on a busy access switch?
explanation: Entries expire before hosts stop sending, so frames for active destinations arrive with no matching table entry. The switch floods those unknown-unicast frames out every port in the VLAN, raising unnecessary traffic and CPU load.

choices.text: More frames are flooded as unknown unicast
The switch stops learning MAC addresses entirely
VLAN traffic is dropped at the trunk
The CPU disables cut-through forwarding

stem: Which forwarding method makes a switch verify a frame's FCS before forwarding it?
explanation: Store-and-forward receives the whole frame, checks the frame check sequence, and discards corrupt frames before forwarding. Cut-through begins forwarding after reading the destination MAC, which lowers latency but propagates errors.

choices.text: Store-and-forward
Cut-through
Fragment-free
Fast-forward

stem: Which VLAN is the native VLAN on an 802.1Q trunk by default?
explanation: Cisco switches use VLAN 1 as the native VLAN unless it is changed. Frames in the native VLAN cross the trunk untagged, which is why best practice is to move the native VLAN to an unused ID on both ends.

choices.text: VLAN 1
VLAN 0
VLAN 1005
VLAN 4095

stem: Why can VLANs 1002 through 1005 not be used for user traffic on a Cisco switch?
explanation: These IDs are reserved by default for legacy FDDI and Token Ring media translations. They appear in the VLAN database but cannot be assigned to access ports or deleted in normal operation.

choices.text: They are reserved for legacy media translations and cannot be assigned
They exceed the 802.1Q tag range
They are reserved for voice traffic only
They are used internally by VTP version 3

stem: A switch port is configured with an access VLAN for a workstation and a voice VLAN for an IP phone. How does the port handle the two traffic types?
explanation: The phone's own voice frames are tagged with the voice VLAN ID, while frames from the attached PC pass through the phone untagged and land in the access VLAN. This lets one port serve both devices without a second cable.

choices.text: Voice frames are tagged; PC frames are untagged in the access VLAN
Both traffic types are untagged in the voice VLAN
PC frames are tagged with the voice VLAN and voice frames are untagged
The port becomes a trunk and drops untagged frames

stem: Which DSCP value corresponds to the Expedited Forwarding per-hop behaviour used to mark voice payload?
explanation: Expedited Forwarding is DSCP 46, written as EF. It maps to the highest-priority queue in most QoS designs, giving voice a low-latency, low-jitter path ahead of data traffic.

stem: Which command limits a switch port to three learned MAC addresses?
explanation: The maximum parameter sets how many secure MAC addresses the port may learn. Once the limit is reached, any additional source MAC triggers the configured violation action.

choices.text: switchport port-security maximum 3
switchport port-security limit 3
switchport port-security mac-address 3
switchport port-security aging 3

stem: Which field of the output from show port-security interface shows how many times the port security rules have been broken?
explanation: The Security Violation Count counter increments each time a frame violates the configured maximum, sticky, or static address rules. It is the quickest way to confirm that a port is actually reacting to an offending device.

choices.text: Security Violation Count
Port Status
Maximum MAC Addresses
Aging Time

stem: Which 802.11 management frame does an access point send to end a client association without implying a security failure?
explanation: A disassociation frame ends an existing association, typically because the AP is rebooting, the client is idle, or the session is being torn down administratively. Deauthentication is a stronger statement that the client is no longer authenticated.

choices.text: Disassociation
Deauthentication
Probe response
Association request

stem: A wireless client is configured for 802.1X but the RADIUS server rejects its credentials. What is the visible result on the client?
explanation: The EAP exchange fails, so the authenticator never moves the port or the wireless session to the authorized state. The client cannot pass traffic even though it may still show the SSID as available or attempt to reconnect.

choices.text: Authentication fails and the client is never authorized to pass traffic
The client falls back to open authentication automatically
The AP assigns a static IP address instead
The client is placed in the voice VLAN

stem: Which information does LLDP-MED add beyond basic LLDP for voice endpoints?
explanation: LLDP-MED defines extensions such as network policy, power over MDI, inventory, and location identification. Network policy is what lets a phone learn its voice VLAN and QoS markings automatically.

choices.text: Network policy, power via MDI, inventory, and location TLVs
A routing table summary for the local subnet
Encrypted CAPWAP tunnel parameters
Spanning-tree topology change notifications

stem: Why should CDP be disabled on ports facing untrusted networks?
explanation: CDP advertisements expose the device model, software version, platform, and management addresses to anyone who can capture them. That information helps an attacker pick exploits and map the topology, so it is suppressed where the neighbour is not trusted.

choices.text: It reveals device model, software version, and management addresses
It consumes enough bandwidth to disrupt voice calls
It prevents STP from converging
It blocks DHCP snooping from binding addresses

stem: An EtherChannel is working, then one member interface is changed to a different speed. What happens to the bundle?
explanation: All members of a bundle must share speed, duplex, and VLAN parameters. A mismatch makes the offending interface incompatible, so it is suspended and removed from the channel, which can reduce total bandwidth or drop the channel if too few members remain.

choices.text: The mismatched interface is suspended and removed from the bundle
The bundle automatically negotiates a common speed
All members drop to half duplex
The channel converts to a routed port

stem: Why must the member interfaces of a Layer 2 EtherChannel be configured consistently before the bundle is relied on?
explanation: The switch validates that members agree on speed, duplex, allowed VLANs, and trunk state. Any disagreement causes the port to be suspended as a bundle mismatch, so the channel silently loses capacity instead of forwarding.

choices.text: Mismatched parameters cause member ports to suspend as bundle inconsistencies
The switch rewrites the configuration of the first member onto the others
STP disables the channel if any member differs
VTP refuses to advertise the VLAN database

stem: Place the 802.1D port states in the order a blocked port passes through them before it forwards traffic.
explanation: A port leaving the blocked state enters listening while it participates in the election, then learning while it populates the MAC table, and only then forwarding. Each transition waits for the forward delay timer, which is why convergence is slow without RSTP.

choices.text: Blocking, listening, learning, forwarding
Blocking, learning, listening, forwarding
Listening, blocking, forwarding, learning
Learning, blocking, listening, forwarding

stem: A storm-control threshold is configured as a percentage of link bandwidth. What happens to the effective threshold if the interface speed is increased?
explanation: The percentage is recalculated against the new link rate, so the same percentage permits a much higher absolute packet or bit rate. A threshold tuned on a 1 Gbps link can allow ten times the traffic after an upgrade to 10 Gbps.

choices.text: The permitted absolute rate rises with the new link speed
The threshold stays fixed in packets per second
Storm control is disabled automatically
The threshold halves to preserve the same absolute rate

stem: Why must an IPv6 static route that uses a link-local next hop also specify the outgoing interface?
explanation: Link-local addresses are only unique within a single link, so the router cannot tell which interface to use from the address alone. Supplying the exit interface makes the route fully specified and removes the ambiguity.

choices.text: A link-local address is only unique on one link, so the exit interface is required
IPv6 does not support next-hop addresses in static routes
The interface is needed only when the next hop is a global address
Without it the route becomes a default route

stem: What is the default administrative distance of a static route that points to a next-hop address?
explanation: A static route with a specified next hop is trusted almost completely and carries AD 1. Only a directly connected route at AD 0 is preferred over it.

stem: How does the forwarding information base differ from the routing information base on a router?
explanation: The RIB is the control-plane table holding every candidate route learned from connected networks, statics, and routing protocols along with their metrics and distances. The FIB is the derived data-plane table containing only the selected best route for each prefix, and it is what actually drives packet forwarding.

choices.text: The RIB holds all candidate routes; the FIB holds only the selected best paths used for forwarding
The RIB holds only connected routes; the FIB holds learned routes
The FIB is populated before the RIB during convergence
The RIB is used for IPv6 and the FIB for IPv4

stem: What does the command show ip route ospf display?
explanation: The command filters the routing table to entries whose source is OSPF, showing the OSPF code, the advertising router, and the metric. Connected and static routes are omitted.

choices.text: Only routes learned through OSPF
The full OSPF link-state database
Only OSPF neighbor adjacencies
All routes including connected and static

stem: Which command creates a switched virtual interface for VLAN 10?
explanation: The interface vlan 10 command enters SVI configuration, where an IP address can be assigned to provide routing or management access for that VLAN. The SVI is the Layer 3 presence of the VLAN on the switch.

choices.text: interface vlan 10
interface gigabitethernet0/1.10
vlan 10 interface
switchport access vlan 10

stem: An SVI is configured with an IP address and no shutdown, yet it stays down/down. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: An SVI only comes up when at least one port in that VLAN is up and forwarding, or when the VLAN itself is active on the switch. Without a live access port or trunk carrying the VLAN, there is nothing to bring the interface up.

choices.text: No active port is assigned to that VLAN
The SVI needs a default gateway configured
The VLAN must be created with the vlan database command
An SVI cannot carry an IPv4 address

stem: Which command enables OSPFv3 process 1 on a router?
explanation: OSPFv3 is configured through the ipv6 router ospf process command, then interfaces are enabled with ipv6 ospf 1 area under each interface. OSPFv3 runs over IPv6 and uses link-local addresses for adjacencies.

choices.text: ipv6 router ospf 1
router ospf 1
router ipv6 ospf 1
ospfv3 1 enable

stem: Two routers have OSPFv3 configured on a shared link but form no adjacency. The area IDs match and the link is up. What should be checked next?
explanation: OSPFv3 requires the per-interface instance ID to match between neighbours; a mismatch means the packets belong to different OSPFv3 instances and are ignored. Unlike OSPFv2, the process ID is local, but the interface instance ID must agree.

choices.text: The OSPFv3 instance ID on both interfaces
The OSPFv2 process ID on both routers
The IPv4 subnet mask on the link
The global unicast address of each router

stem: Which single summary route covers 192.168.0.0/24 through 192.168.3.0/24?
explanation: The four /24 networks share the first 22 bits, so they aggregate into 192.168.0.0/22. That block spans 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.3.255 and replaces four separate advertisements with one.

stem: On an OSPF ASBR, which command summarizes redistributed external routes before they are advertised into the OSPF domain?
explanation: The summary-address command is applied in router configuration on the ASBR and creates a single aggregate for a range of external prefixes. Internal area summarization instead uses the area range command on an ABR.

choices.text: summary-address
area range
ip summary-address eigrp
auto-summary

stem: Two OSPF routers are connected by a working link but are configured in different areas. What is the result?
explanation: OSPF requires both ends of a link to agree on the area ID before they can become neighbours. A mismatch keeps them from progressing past the initial hello exchange, so no adjacency forms and no routes are exchanged.

choices.text: No adjacency forms because the area IDs must match on the link
The routers become neighbours but exchange no Type 1 LSAs
The link is treated as an external connection automatically
The router with the higher router ID becomes the ABR

stem: On a broadcast multi-access OSPF segment, a router shows a neighbour stuck in 2WAY/DROTHER. Is this a fault?
explanation: On broadcast and NBMA networks, routers that are neither the DR nor the BDR stay in 2WAY with each other by design. Only a neighbour that should be DR or BDR remaining in 2WAY, or a point-to-point link showing it, indicates a problem.

choices.text: No; non-DR and non-BDR routers stay in 2WAY on broadcast segments by design
Yes; every neighbour must reach FULL
Yes; it means the hello timers differ
No; 2WAY means the neighbour is the DR

stem: Which protocol resolves an IPv6 address to a link-layer address, and which messages does it use?
explanation: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery performs address resolution with Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages carried in ICMPv6. It replaces IPv4 ARP and also handles router discovery and duplicate address detection.

choices.text: Neighbor Discovery, using neighbour solicitation and advertisement messages
ARP, using broadcast requests and unicast replies
DHCPv6, using solicit and advertise messages
RARP, using the broadcast address

stem: A DHCP client sends a DHCPRELEASE message. What is it telling the server?
explanation: DHCPRELEASE is sent when a client gives up its address, for example at shutdown or when the interface goes down. The server can then return the address to the pool instead of holding it until the lease expires.

choices.text: It is giving up the lease and the address can be returned to the pool
It is requesting an extension of the current lease
It is declining an address because of a conflict
It is asking for additional configuration parameters

stem: What does the log keyword add to an access control entry?
explanation: The log keyword makes the router generate a syslog message each time a packet matches that entry, recording the source, destination, and action. It is a troubleshooting aid and should be used sparingly because logging every match can consume significant CPU.

choices.text: A syslog message for each packet matching the entry
A counter that resets after each match
An automatic deny rule for the same traffic
Encryption of the matching packets

stem: In a DHCP snooping deployment, which port should be configured as trusted?
explanation: The port leading toward the legitimate DHCP server or relay is trusted so its offer and acknowledgement messages are allowed. All client-facing ports stay untrusted, which blocks a rogue server from handing out addresses.

choices.text: The port facing the legitimate DHCP server or relay
Every access port attached to an end device
Only the trunk ports between switches
The port attached to the default gateway

stem: What does the outside global address represent in a NAT translation table?
explanation: The outside global address is the address of the external host as it appears on the internet side of the translation. It is distinct from the outside local address, which is how that same host appears to the inside network.

choices.text: The external host's address as seen on the internet side
The internal host's address before translation
The public address assigned to the internal host
The router interface address used as the default gateway

stem: What is the default Dynamic ARP Inspection rate limit on an untrusted interface?
explanation: Untrusted ports are limited to 15 ARP packets per second by default so that a flood of ARP traffic cannot overwhelm the switch's inspection process. The limit can be raised or lowered per interface with ip arp inspection limit.

choices.text: 15 packets per second
1 packet per second
100 packets per second
Unlimited

stem: Which command copies the running configuration to a TFTP server?
explanation: The copy command takes a source and a destination, so copy running-config tftp: prompts for the server address and filename. TFTP runs over UDP 69, so the transfer is unencrypted and should be confined to a management network.

choices.text: copy running-config tftp:
backup running-config tftp:
write tftp: running-config
export running-config tftp:

stem: Which statement correctly compares ESP and AH in IPsec?
explanation: ESP can encrypt the payload and also authenticate it, which is why it is used for most IPsec deployments. AH authenticates the packet including the outer IP header but provides no confidentiality, so it cannot hide the data.

choices.text: ESP can provide encryption and authentication; AH provides authentication only
AH provides encryption; ESP provides authentication only
Both provide encryption but AH also compresses the payload
ESP authenticates the outer header while AH does not

stem: What does a controller's northbound REST API allow a management platform to do?
explanation: The REST API exposes controller functions as HTTP resources, so an external system can read inventory, pull telemetry, and push configuration changes programmatically. That is what makes integration with automation and monitoring platforms possible without screen scraping.

choices.text: Read inventory and telemetry and push configuration changes programmatically
Replace the need for device-level credentials entirely
Bypass the controller's policy engine for urgent changes
Convert CAPWAP tunnels into GRE tunnels

stem: Why does a controller-based design make policy consistency easier than managing each device individually?
explanation: The controller holds the intended configuration and pushes it to every managed device, so a single change propagates uniformly. Device-by-device management invites drift, where one switch keeps an old ACL or VLAN because it was missed during a change window.

choices.text: One policy definition is pushed to all managed devices, preventing configuration drift
The controller removes the need for any device configuration
Devices inherit policy only after a reboot
Each device pulls a unique policy generated for its model

stem: When asking a model to modify an existing device configuration, why is requesting a diff better than requesting the full config?
explanation: A diff keeps the output short enough to review line by line and limits the change to the intended lines. A full configuration invites unrelated rewrites, makes review impractical, and increases the chance that an accidental omission breaks the device.

choices.text: It keeps the output reviewable and limits changes to the intended lines
It lets the model skip validating the existing configuration
It guarantees the model will not hallucinate commands
It removes the need for a change window
